item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract and has much lower review risk, although it still needs revision before merge because Upload duplicates Add instead of routing through it and lacks a source-reader failure test.","reasons":["Both candidates correctly add the required Upload signature, use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validate empty filename/nil content, and verify multipart encoding and retry behavior.","Both violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add; each duplicates Add's option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error logic.","B additionally changes RawClient.Do body ownership, seeking, content-length, and retry behavior across the SDK, directly conflicting with the contract's instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery or change Add behavior.","B's shared io.ReadSeeker-based GetBody closure introduces broader correctness and concurrency concerns because every replay operates on the same mutable reader rather than producing an independent body reader instance. That machinery is unnecessary for the contracted solution because multipartbody.NewFile already buffers the upload body by design and should be passed to Add via UploadFrom B's implementation tests an os.File source and identical multipart bytes across attempts, but this advantage does not justify its prohibited transport-level semantic expansion.and A's narrower implementation is easier to correct: replace its duplicated request block with a call to s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...)."],"risks_a":["Upload does not call FilesService.Add, so future Add changes could diverge from Upload behavior.","Tests do not cover an input reader that fails while multipartbody.NewFile is consuming it.","The retry test supplies bytes.NewReader rather than a more clearly forward-only or streamed source, weakening verification that Upload buffering—not source replayability—is what enables retries."],"risks_b":["Makes an expressly out-of-scope RawClient.Do retry/body-ownership change affecting Raw, Add, Update, and other SDK consumers.","The GetBody closure reuses one mutable io.ReadSeeker, which is less robust than returning independent readers and may behave poorly under concurrent or overlapping replay scenarios.","Upload still duplicates FilesService.Add rather than routing through it as required.Because req.Body is replaced with io.NopCloser(rs), this changes whether caller-provided bodies are closed, an API semantic change beyond the task.tests include no source-reader failure case despite the contract explicitly requiring one."]}
